chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a Christian who testified upon a testimony, then became a Muslim afterwards, would his testimony be allowed? He said: Yes. He is in a position to testify.
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a Christian valid if they convert to Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that a Christian who converts to Islam retains the legal validity of his testimony, affirming that his prior status as *Ahl al-Kitab* does not disqualify him. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that conversion purifies the individual's standing without retroactively invalidating their capacity to bear witness, a key point in *Fiqh al-Shahadat*. The Imam’s concise response underscores the continuity of legal competence across religious transitions within the Islamic community.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Muhammad Bin Humran, 
(The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a Christian who testified upon a testimony, then became a Muslim afterwards, would his testimony be allowed?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. He is in a position to testify’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Najran from Muhammad ibn Humran who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a Christian man who bears a testimony, then becomes a Muslim if his testimony is acceptable.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he is in the right position to testify.’”
